entity_ranked_evidence.snippet: * Edit&action=edit "Edit this page [e]"). **Alimuddin** (Urdu: **علیم الدین**‎; 15 December 1930 – 12 July 2012) was a Pakistani cricketer who played 25 Tests for Pakistan between 1954 and 1962. In international cricket, he scored 1,091 runs "Run (cricket)") at the average "Batting average (cricket)") of 25.37, including two centuries "Century (cricket)") and seven fifties. In 1954, he was a member of the Pakistani squad which toured England and recorded Pakistan's first Test match win. [edit&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: First-class career")]. Alimuddin played 25 Test matches for Pakistan during his career and scored 1,091 runs in international cricket at the average of 25.37. Alimuddin started his international career against England in June 1954, at the Lord's Cricket Ground, in a match in which he scored 19 runs. In 1954–55, he played, against India, in Pakistan's first home Tests, finishing the series as the leading run scorer with 332; he made three fifties and in the fifth match scored 103 not out at the National Stadium, Karachi, his first international century.
